subject: Mathematics
central_question: How can ordinary differential equations be classified and solved to obtain general or condition-specific functions?
in_scope_units: 9.1 Introduction: differential equations as equations involving derivatives.
9.2 Basic Concepts: ordinary differential equations, order and degree.
9.3 General and Particular Solutions of a Differential Equation.
9.4 Methods of Solving First Order, First Degree Differential Equations.

known_pitfalls.claim: Order is the highest power of a derivative.
known_pitfalls.correction: Order is the order of the highest derivative present.
Degree is defined only when the equation is polynomial in derivatives.

known_pitfalls.claim: A particular solution contains arbitrary constants.
known_pitfalls.correction: A particular solution is free from arbitrary constants after conditions determine them.
Separation works only when the equation can be rearranged into a function of y times dy equal to a function of x times dx.

recommended_example_progression: Use NCERT Example 1 to identify order and degree.
Use NCERT Example 2 or 3 to verify a proposed solution.
Use NCERT Example 4 for a variable-separable general solution.
Use a linear-equation example with integrating factor e^(integral P dx).
ncert_end_of_chapter_exercises_reference: The chapter contains Exercises 9.1 onward for classification, verification and first-order solution methods, followed by the Miscellaneous Exercise on Chapter 9.
